page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-16GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 8 shared vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 1 thread per core, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not bundle local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a varied profile. While Geekbench single-core and text processing tests show strong results in the top 25%, stress-ng single-core performance falls into the bottom 10%, and multi-core performance is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is also mixed; small-block read-only cached bandwidth is average, but large-block uncached read and write speeds are weak. Similarly, Passmark memory scores are in the bottom 25%, while Passmark CPU and database operations maintain average performance.

Given its shared CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server represents a budget-friendly option for workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated CPU performance. It is suited for static web serving, basic Redis key-value operations, and lightweight text or image processing. However, it is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM inference, where its uncached memory bandwidth and shared CPU resources present performance tradeoffs.
